newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke still expects to hit 2.5 pct inflation.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke still expects to hit 2.5 pct inflation.

text.p: UK Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Wednesday that he still expected to meet his government's target of 2.5 percent for underlying inflation.
"If you look at overall picture of Britain's economy, (there is) good steady growth," Clarke told reporters. "This will keep us on target for inflation of 2.5 pct of less."
Clarke said that the level of earnings remained stable, producer prices were at an "astonishingly low level historically" and Britain was also experiencing an "extremely strong exchange rate".
He declined to make any comment on interest rates or on the testimony given by Bank of England Governor Eddie George to the the Treasury select committee on Monday.

Commenting on retail sales data for January, which showed a 0.6 percent month-on-month rise versus a 0.8 percent fall in December, Clarke said they showed "pretty steady growth, in line with forecasts made at the time of the budget".
